summary: Port Burwell's Historic 1840 Lighthouse, the oldest wooden lighthouse on Lake Erie's Canadian shore, was kept by the Sutherland family for over a century and closed to visitors in 2023.

lens.note: LighthouseFriends says a Fresnel lens is still in the lantern; the order of that lens is not stated. A fourth-order dioptric apparatus replaced the lamps and reflectors in 1910 (LighthouseFriends; Department report for the year to 31 March 1910, pp. 100-101). The register dates a Fresnel dioptric lens to about 1900 ("around the turn of the century").

structures.note: 45 ft in the 1876 inspection as LighthouseFriends quotes it; the Historical Society says more than 65 ft above the ground. The station record's 14.0 m is near 45 ft.

access.note: Closed to the public since 2023, when the structure was declared unsafe. Stabilization measures are in place. The Marine Museum across the street (20 Pitt Street) is open seasonally.

visit.note: Museum across the street at 20 Pitt Street, open daily from Victoria Day weekend to Labour Day.

facts.agency: Port Burwell Historical Society (legal owner and sole steward after council approved the transfer on 30 July 2026; symbolic key handed over 31 July 2026); the Municipality of Bayham owned it from 1998 until then

events.note: Wooden tower completed by Alexander Saxon
Alexander Sutherland keeper; the Sutherland family kept the light until 1962, apart from 1952 to 1955
Alexander Sutherland, Jr. appointed keeper on 7 May 1874
Breakwater piers at the harbour mouth extended by the Department of Public Works (1899 per LighthouseFriends; the 1900 report shows the work in progress)
Fourth-order dioptric apparatus, petroleum vapour under an incandescent mantle, replaces three lamps and reflectors (LighthouseFriends; Department report for the year to 31 March 1910, pp. 100-101)
Department takes over the two range lights on the east pier, set up by the car-ferry company in 1906
Unwatched dioptric light established at the outer end of the west breakwater (harbour light, not the tower)
Diaphone fog alarm on the east pier, 1 November 1917 (harbour fog alarm, not the tower)
Diaphone discontinued; electric fog alarm established on the west pierhead
Acquired by the Village of Port Burwell from the federal government in April 1965
Partial restoration through a Local Initiatives Program grant
Heritage property under village bylaw No. 85-29
Major restoration from July 1986 by Mennonite craftsmen using hand tools; virtually all long beams replaced with Douglas fir
Ceremonial relighting of the restored tower, 20 June 1987
Ownership passes to the Municipality of Bayham on amalgamation of 1 January 1998
Structure declared unsafe; closed to the public
Declared surplus 25 June 2026; council resolution 30 July 2026; symbolic key handed to the Historical Society 31 July 2026

corrections.why: No source we read names a Bayham Historical Society. The Port Burwell Historical Society became owner and steward on 31 July 2026, after the Municipality of Bayham owned the lighthouse from 1998.
The tower has been closed to the public since 2023, when the structure was declared unsafe. The Bayham page says it is not currently open to visitors.
The register and LighthouseFriends both give 1962 as the year the light went out of service. No source we read gives 1963 for the tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Two sources disagree and the story says so: LighthouseFriends, quoting the 1876 inspection, gives 45 ft; the Historical Society says more than 65 ft above the ground. The record's 14.0 m fits the 45 ft figure. Not settled.

notes_for_editor: Keepers: the roster is LighthouseFriends alone. The 1906 list (p. 165, scan p. 174) and the 1911 list (p. 248, scan p. 255) were both checked on the page images: 'Sutherland, Jno' sits on the Port Burwell row, and 'John Sutherland' on the Port Burwell, Inner Range row. Neither entry settles a span; they confirm the family at the station. John Sutherland's span: 44 years on the roster (1895-1939), 45 in a granddaughter's 1987 account (as LighthouseFriends prints it); not reconciled. Height: 45 ft (1876 inspection via LF), more than 65 ft (Society), 14.0 m in the record; unresolved. Lens: the register dates a Fresnel dioptric lens to about 1900; LF and the 1910 Department report (pp. 100-101, paragraph text) give a fourth-order apparatus in 1910; the surviving lens's order is not stated. The record's 1963 deactivation has no source here (corrected to 1962 in corrections). The record's agency name is corrected. Access: the record says public; the tower has been closed since 2023. Nothing sourced for storms, wrecks or rescues tied to this tower was found in the pages read, so that chapter is omitted; Canadian newspapers were not searched. The Prothero passages are copyrighted; the story paraphrases them, attributed to the Society's page, and the evidence quotes are internal. Museum hours: the Bayham page reads 'closed for the season' at checking; the story gives its seasonal schedule. The NT page's 2022-2023 comment about paint sealing moisture is not used. Position: the record (OSM) is 42.645298, -80.806895; LighthouseFriends gives 42.64373, -80.80685 (about 180 m apart); not changed. The 1998 register sentence is the Historic Sites Board minutes; no conflict noted there.
